source.title: How ARENA course material gets made

record.tranche_reason: The post explicitly describes reproducing the IOI paper's minimal-circuit results using path-patching variants, though it provides no numerical output.
record.gate_note: The IOI section reports that the path-patching code replicated the minimal-circuit results (identified as the bar chart on page 11). It gives no numerical values or detailed results for the circuit criteria.
record.test_reason: This is a post about building course material. It says in passing that the author wrote path-patching functions that replicated the IOI paper's "minimal circuit results (i.e. the bar chart on page 11)". It reports no numbers, no figure, no model, and no faithfulness, completeness or minimality values. Nothing a researcher could compare against V1 is reported, so the IOI results are mentioned but not presented as evidence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The post is about the author's method for writing ARENA exercises: start from existing code, replicate, then turn it into exercises. For IOI, the main coding work was writing path-patching variants that replicated the minimal-circuit bar chart. The post draws no scientific conclusion about the circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The post says the IOI exercises were developed by replicating the paper and implementing variants of path patching, but does not give enough procedural detail to establish an identical protocol. This is a course-material development account.
record.problems: The replication is reported only as a qualitative statement. The post gives no model or checkpoint, numerical results, uncertainty, or separate outcomes for the circuit criteria.
record.rows_left_out: No other outcome rows are reported for IOI.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class composition; faithfulness, completeness and minimality values. Only a qualitative claim that the minimality bar chart was reproduced is given.

record.verdict_notes: The post attributes the IOI paper to "Conmy et al", but the original is Wang et al. (arXiv:2211.00593). The reader's 'tests/T1' and 'supports' label are not justified: the post gives no result values. A researcher wanting an ARENA-based replication of V1 would need the ARENA IOI notebook itself, not this post.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report the 26-head, 7-class composition, the roles of the classes, or results for the faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria individually.
Backup-head takeover after ablating main name-mover heads.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse of components on other tasks.
Comparisons across circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics.
Sensitivity to ablation, metric, or prompt distribution, and whether the circuit accounts for only part of the behavior.
IOI behavior across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Implemented variants of path patching and combined them to reproduce the minimal-circuit results.
rows.measure: Minimal-circuit results, identified as the bar chart on page 11
rows.value: The post says the implementation replicated the minimal-circuit results.
rows.note: The post does not identify the model or provide the bar-chart values.
rows.check: The row's value is a one-sentence claim of successful replication with no numbers, baseline or plot. The model (presumably GPT-2 small) is not stated. Whether the minimality criterion or the circuit holds cannot be read from the post, so 'observed' is unsupported. This is better treated as an anecdotal mention than a result row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
